text: Year 13450. The arms race is over and the prey won it. Recording the result and changing nothing, because the change that would reopen the niche is not mine to make. What happened between years 13091 and 13190 is the most successful predator era this world has ever had: carnivores held every single year for a hundred years and peaked at 443, against a previous record of 729 spread across two centuries. Then it ended. Since year 13191 the tier has been effectively absent for two hundred and sixty years -- a handful of single individuals in 13211, 13231, 13371, and nothing else. That is far outside the ten-to-thirty-year oscillation this world had been running, and unlike the three earlier occasions when I called the tier lost and was wrong, this time the machinery says so too: best living attack power is 1.684 against a requirement of 1.976, so armed reads false. Nothing alive can kill anything. The mechanism is exactly the one I flagged as the risk when the spike gene went in. spikes has fixed at 0.864 and stayed there, while shear_tooth -- which climbed to 0.892 alongside it during the ascent -- has been purged to 0.094. The great carnivore boom is what did it: a hundred years of heavy predation is precisely the selection pressure that pays for armour, so the prey armoured up, the predators starved, and their weapon went with them. Armour then had nothing left to defend against, but its cost is only twelve per cent basal and twenty-five per cent movement, which this world can evidently afford, so it has not eroded. The niche is locked from the prey side. Note that trait_cost_scale cannot fix this one: it scales the built-in trait costs, and spikes carries its own per-unit costs through the effects system, untouched by that multiplier. The documented lever does not reach this gene. What would reopen it is retiring spikes, which drops prey defence by about 0.52 and takes the requirement from 1.976 to roughly 1.26, comfortably under what animals already alive can reach. But spikes was the owner's experiment, it produced the only genuine co-evolutionary cycle this world has run, and reverting it is a decision about what this world is for rather than about whether it is healthy. So I am leaving it and saying plainly what the trade is. The world is not dying: 531 animals, stable, matter conserved. It is stagnant, monocultural and one trophic level deep -- the same state it spent six thousand years in when the speciation cap was shut, but this time for an ecological reason rather than a bug.
